Document: Do I need car insurance?

Many cars from Ukraine are only insured within Ukraine.

This means that you need to take out a separate insurance if you are using your car in the Netherlands.  

For most recent information see: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100128-having-your-own-car-in-the-netherlands

Document: Where can I find shelter when arriving in the Netherlands?  

Links to the Red Cross Website  On the Red Cross Website you can now find updated information regarding the shelter process for Ukrainian refugees.

Click on the following links for the [English](https://www.rodekruis.nl/english-information/), [Ukrainian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/ukrainian/) and the [Russian](https://www.rodekruis.nl/russian/) version of this webpage.

You can always share these links with the PA as well.

See also below what the general explanation is.   

General advice  If you want to apply for Temporary Protection and need help with a shelter place, visit a municipality ("gemeente" in Dutch).

Municipalities register displaced Ukrainians and help find housing.

(Please check the latest Temporary Protection rules on [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100187-chtoby-poluchit-vremennuyu-zashchitu-vy-dolzhny-sootvetstvovat-etim-usloviyam).)

Document: How can I travel from Ukraine to the Netherlands?  

Unfortunately, we cannot provide you with information on fleeing routes.   

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has set up information and support hotlines for persons in Ukraine and fleeing Ukraine in different countries.

The number depends from which country you call.

You can look on their website to see which number you have to call: https://www.iom.int/ukraine-iom-hotlines-garyachi-linii-mom-persons-affected-war  You can find an overview of organsations that can possibly help you travel from Ukraine to The Netherlands:  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100130-travelling-from-ukraine-to-the-netherlands

Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

This applies to both refugees who have been in the Netherlands for some time and new arrivals.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.   

[*Dutch Government website*](https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay)

Document: Can I get shelter in the Netherlands if I am already registered in another Schengen country?

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Document: Falling through the ice In the Netherlands the water in ditches, lakes and ponds can freeze when the temperature is below zero degrees Celsius.

A layer of ice then forms on the water.

If the ice is thick enough you can walk and skate on it.    

If the ice is not thick enough you can fall through it.

This is very dangerous.

You can get hypothermia, drown or even die.   

Only go out on the ice if you are sure it is thick enough.

Also, never go out on the ice alone.

Call for help if someone has fallen through the ice or call 112 in a life-threatening situation.

Watch your own safety if you want to rescue someone who has fallen through the ice.   

Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/ice-and-skating

Document: Water and swimming There is a lot of water in the Netherlands.

Therefore, it is important that you can swim.

Even if you can swim, there are still risks to be considered:   - the bottom is often uneven   - it can sometimes be unexpectedly deep, making you suddenly unable to stand   - cold water can give you cramps   - strong currents can carry you away     Always be careful, even when the weather is nice and calm:   - do not swim if you cannot swim   - always keep a close eye on children   - never swim alone and do not swim in places where it is prohibited     Source and more information: https://www.mycoa.nl/en/the-netherlands/dangers-in-nature/water-and-swimming

Document: You can register at any municipality, either in person or sometimes by email.

After registration, the municipality will help with housing.

If the municipality has space, they will help you.

If not, they will contact the Regional Coordination Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("RCVS"), which may escalate to the National Centre for Refugee Dispersal ("LCVS").

Please check details [here](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/ru/ukrainian-refugee/article/100179-chto-neobhodimo-sdelat-po-pribytii-v-niderlandy)  

Due to the limited number of available shelter places, the Dutch government asks Ukrainians to find their own housing if possible.

If you can’t, go to the municipality for help.  

It’s a good idea to ask the municipality for written confirmation of your visit.

If they’re unable to help immediately, kindly ask if a temporary solution can be provided while they search for a place for you.   

Actions to take when general advice is not sufficient If the general advice isn’t enough, forward the case to the team captain.  

Important disclaimer Because this process is centrally organized, the above procedure must be followed.

Document: Can I study here?  

Refugees from Ukraine and third-country nationals covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can study at a university or college in the Netherlands, provided they have the required prior education level and meet the admission requirements for the course they want to follow.  

- Go to nuffic.nl to see how your previous education in Ukraine compares to the Dutch education system.  

- Request a free credential evaluation from IDW.

- Study in NL provides more general information about Dutch education system and to seek training.

- If you have found a suitable course, please contact the educational institution directly about your registration.

Please note that the deadline for applying for a course at a university or college is generally May 1st.

For MBO courses, the deadline is usually April 1st.

The deadline may be earlier for certain courses with additional requirements.  

The Dutch government brochure also provides information about studying at an institution of higher education in the Netherlands.  

Refugees from Ukraine can also follow a MBO course, but most MBO courses require a high level of Dutch.   

For the most recent information, see:  https://www.uaf.nl/en/oekraine/

Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

In general, houses are expensive, because there is a large housing shortage in the Netherlands, especially in the larger cities.   

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.  

Places where private homes are offered: Funda, AirBNB, Marktplaats website, Facebook groups per city (search for 'I'm looking for a home').   

For most recent information see: [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing)  and [renting a house](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house)

testCases.input: I am undocumented and I have two children. They need to go to school but I am afraid to register them. Also, where can I get winter clothes for them? They are growing fast
testCases.actualOutput:
Hello! I am Aidly, the HIA chatbot.

Regarding your children going to school: All children in the Netherlands have to attend school regardless of their residence status, including undocumented children. Children from the age of 4 can attend school, and they must go until they are 18 and have obtained a diploma. You can register your children at any school, and there are special classes to help them learn Dutch if needed. So, even if you are undocumented, your children have the right to education.

For more information about education for children from Ukraine, you can watch this video by the Red Cross: https://youtu.be/ERDDxnwB4K4

About winter clothes: You can find support for clothing through the Red Cross Helpful Information website, which provides an overview of clothing options available in different cities. You can check https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ for places where you can get clothes or buy them at a low price.

If you want, I can help you find specific locations near you for clothing support.

If you have any other questions or need assistance, feel free to ask!

Document: Remaining Undocumented If you remain in the Netherlands without residency status you will become *undocumented*.

Undocumented persons do not have a right to housing, work or government subsidies.

However, you still have the right to necesarry medical care, judicial assistance and children under 18 have to right to attend school as well.  

You can choose to apply for asylum at any point with undocumented status.  

For more information you can reach out to the Red Cross helpline via Whatsapp here: https://wa.me/31614458781 or visit the Red Cross website Helpful Information: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/

Document: Can my child go to school?  

All children in the Netherlands have to attend school, regardless of their residence status.

In principle, children from the age of 4 can already attend school.

In The Netherlands, children must go to school until they are 18 years old and have obtained a diploma.  

You can register your child at any school.

The school will decide if your child will be admitted.

There are special intermediary classes where children can first learn the Dutch language.  

For an information video made by the Red Cross see:  EN: https://youtu.be/ERDDxnwB4K4  UA: https://youtu.be/RSbzdPYOFPk

RUS: https://youtu.be/qwxgVeHB0Pk  

For the most recent information, see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/education  https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100007-education-for-children-from-ukraine-who-cannot-speak-dutch-yet

Document: Can my children finish primary or secondary school?

Is a minor still entitled to education during the departure period?

All children under 18 have the right to education, regardless of their status.

As long as they reside in the Netherlands and are enrolled in school, they can continue their education.      

Students who were already enrolled at a Dutch educational institution before 4 March 2024 according to the applicable rules will be allowed to complete their studies.

What is important   here is that there was lawful residence in the Netherlands   at the time of enrolment.

This does not discharge them from their obligation to leave the Netherlands.

Enrolment at a Dutch institution of higher education does not confer lawful residence.

Non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit in Ukraine who are not lawfully residing in the Netherlands on 4 March 2024 may not start a new course.

Document: What are the steps I should take to register a child travelling alone from Ukraine?  

Unaccompanied minor foreingers are children who are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands, are under the age of 18 when they arrive in the Netherlands and came without their parents.   

Firstly, unaccompanied Ukrainian children should always be registered with the municipality (like all other refugees from Ukraine) so that they are inculded in the Basic Registration Persons (BRP) and do not get out of sight.  

When the municipality determines that a minor is unaccompanied, Nidos should be contacted immediately.

Then, Nidos does an intake with the minor, and if possible, remotely with parents.

Nidos assesses whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

The municipality can report the minor to Nidos via 088-5011885 or oekraine@nidos.nl.  

For all children, shelter must be arranged in the Netherlands.

Nidos is responsible for the shelter of unaccompanied minors.

Nidos arranges shelter in host families, preferably with the same cultural background.

Document: My municipality still hasn't arranged any participation for school for my children.

What should we do?  

Every municipality has its own tempo with fixing problems.

Somewhere it takes few days, in other cases it takes few weeks.

Anyway, your children will get the same rights for education as well as Dutch children do.

At the moment you can start with self-studying English and Dutch languages.   

Here we can advise you some of useful applications:  1.

Gramaro - the application has opened free access for a year for Ukrainians.

You can learn English grammar for free;   2.

LingQ - is a program for learning languages (46 available languages).

To get free access, you need to contact the support service and write that you are from Ukraine;   

3.

Drops - opened a premium for a year for Ukrainians.

Convenient and quick vocabulary learning (the most important thing if you went abroad);   4.

Busuu - opened access to a premium subscription for 3 months for Ukrainians. 13 languages available;   5.

Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I do not have documents?  

Without documents you can currently not register for the BRP.   

When you have the Ukrainian nationality but cannot prove this with documents (ID or passport), you should contact the Ukrainian embassy in The Hague.

They may be able to get proof of your identity and nationality.

The embassy can issue an identifying certificate that can be used to register for the BRP at the municpality.   Children from Ukraine without proof of identification can be registered with their parents at the municipality.

In the absence of documents, parents can make a statement on oath establishing the identity of the children.

The children are then registered by the municipality together with the parents.   

Address Ukrainian Embassy:  Zeestraat 78, 2518 AD The Hague  Open from Monday to Friday between 09:00 and 13:00 Telephone: +31 (70) 360 72 18  Email: emb_nl@mfa.gov.ua.

https://netherlands.mfa.gov.ua/en   

For the most recent information see: https://ind.nl/en/ukraine/temporary-protection-directive-ukraine

Document: How can I register for Basic Registration of Persons (BRP)?  

You can register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) at the municipality you are staying.   

When you register for the BRP at the municipality, your registration is automatically referred to the Immigration & Naturalization Service (IND).

The IND is responsible for the process that establishes your temporary protected status.

Refugees from Ukraine that are registered at the IND will receive temporary protection and are allowed to stay at least until 4 March 2027.

This might be extended to a maximum of 3 years.  

After registering with the municipality, you will receive a citizen service number (BSN).

You will need this number for health care, education, work and financial matters (for example, opening a bank account).

When you received your BSN, you can apply for a DigiD.

You can use this to access online government services.

Document: Who is responsible for the shelter of children travelling alone from Ukraine?

Children travelling alone from Ukraine also have to go to the municipality to get Temporary Protection.

They always have to get shelter right away.

The municipality has to call with Nidos.

Nidos then conducts an intake with the minor—and, where possible, remotely with the parents—to determine whether applying for temporary guardianship is appropriate.

Document: Can I register for the Basic Registration of Persons (BRP) when I fled from Ukraine but I have another nationality?  

This depends on whether you have a permanent residence permit.

Only displaced persons from Ukraine who are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive can register with the BRP.

As of July 19, non-Ukrainians with a temporary residence permit for Ukraine can no longer apply for temporary protection.

This means that if you have a temporary residence permit, you cannot register with the BRP.

Document: How does the appointment to collect my proof of residency work and what do I have to fill in?  

At the pickup location, an IND staff member will check:  - your registration with the local council/municipality - your appointment code - your documents - whether you fall under the Temporary Protection Directive.  

You must fill in 2 IND forms during your appointment.

At the reception location you will find a translation of both forms into Ukrainian, Russian and English.

There are also employees who can help you fill in these forms.

They speak Ukrainian, Russian or English.   

Form 1: Asylum application (applicable for age => 15): The official asylum application (minors – together with parents on the form).  

Form 2: Antecedents certificate (applicable for age => 12): On this certificate, you state whether you have ever committed a punishable offence or crime.   

Because you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, your rights will be different to those of the standard asylum application.

You can work in the Netherlands immediately.

The IND will not assess your application for asylum while the directive is in force.

The directive will apply at least until 4 March 2027.

Document: Is daycare for my child for free?  

No, daycare is not free.

There are, however, a number of possibilities to receive a reimbursement through the city council.  

Toddlers are entitled to a certain number hours of free daycare or education.  

The city council can also give a family a so-called social medical indication ("SMI"), which can cover daycare costs if necessary.

The city council is responsible for assigning the indication.  

Research is done to find ways to make daycare more financially accessible for displaced persons from Ukraine working in the Netherlands.

Document: My host family/friends/family where I am staying does not allow me to register myself, what should I do?  

It is very important to be registered at an adress in the Netherlands.

If you are not registered, you cannot get Temporary Protection.

If you registered on an adress before, got the Temporary Protection but deregistered lateron, you can lose the Temporary Protection status because it seems you left the country.

Also social benefits are connected to your adress.  

Hosts can register refugees from Ukraine without for example losing their social benefits.

Maybe your hosts are afraid it has negative effects on their own financial situation, but this is often not the case.   

If the host won't register the PA, it is best to refer the PA to a municipality shelter or advise them to find other housing where they can register.  

Always check with the PA how long he/she can still stay with the host family/friends/relatives and make sure PA won't be on the street.

If you think this is the case, refer the case to the TC.   

You can check if there is an organization in the town that you stay in that can give free legal advice about this issue (see category 'Administrative').

Document: Can I receive child benefit?  

If you are a displaced person from Ukraine, you are entitled to supplementary child benefit.

Child benefit is a financial contribution to help cover the costs of raising a child.

Whether you are eligible for a benefit and, if so, to what amount, depends on your situation.

If you have one or more children under the age of 18, you may be eligible for child benefit.

The amount you receive depends on the age of your child, not on your income.

You are only eligible for healthcare benefit and supplementary child benefit when you are working.

This is an additional condition for displaced persons from Ukraine.

Because you hold temporary protection status, you are allowed to work in the Netherlands.

Below you will find more information on what facilities should be present at the different types of reception.

Document: Public shelter If you are covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, you keep your right to reception.

The reception is a joint responsibility of all Dutch municipalities and Safety Regions.

In the first place you report to the municipality in which you are registered with a request for a place in the municipal reception facilities.

If there is no room (or no longer any room), the 'registering municipality' will contact the safety region.

The safety region will see if there is a place available in the region.

If that is not the case, the safety region submits a request for trans-regional relocation to the KCIO (Ukraine Coordination Information Office).

Document: Do I have to pay for shelter if I have an income?

Starting July 1st 2024, displaced people from Ukraine with a job or their own income must help pay for their reception in a municipality.

You will no longer receive a living allowance.   

Displaced people from Ukraine who have to pay:   -are 18 years old and above.

-are staying in a municipal shelter.    

And who:  -have a job; or -have unemployment benefits; or -have benefits because they are long-term sick or unable to work;  -or receive an allowance.

Document: Can I rent a house?  

You can rent a house from private individuals.

In general, houses are expensive, because there is a large housing shortage in the Netherlands, especially in the larger cities.   

As a displaced person from Ukraine, you will receive living allowance when you stay at a shelter location, both in the municipal shelter and in the private shelter.

If you rent your own independent accommodation, you are no longer entitled to living allowance.  

Places where private homes are offered: Funda, AirBNB, Marktplaats website, Facebook groups per city (search for 'I'm looking for a home').   

For most recent information see: [RefugeeHelp](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100045-permanent-housing)  and [renting a house](https://www.refugeehelp.nl/en/ukrainian-refugee/article/100047-this-is-what-you-need-to-arrange-if-you-rent-a-house)

Document: Can I stay in the public shelter while I have a paid job?  

Displaced persons from Ukraine that are doing paid work may remain at the municipal reception centre.

However, you will have to pay a contribution.

You can also move to other accommodation, for instance with a host family, friends or family members, or at a hotel.  

For most recent information see: https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income

Document: How can I get financial support while I'm in a public shelter?

You get your living allowance from the municipality where you are registered.

You receive the money in their bank account, on a money card, in cash or in goods.  

Living allowance may be payed out in kind by local authorities (for example when meals are offered).

As a result, it is possible that displaced persons in some municipalities receive (much) less living allowance.   

For most recent information see:  https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/work-and-income

Document: Requesting shelter upon arrival in the NL as required by Dutch law.

*Cited directly from the Dutch government website*:  It is very difficult at the moment for local authorities to arrange accomodation.

The authorities’ priority is to ensure accommodation for the most vulnerable refugees.

Refugees from Ukraine who are able to, are being asked to make every effort to find a place of residence by themselves.

This applies to both refugees who have been in the Netherlands for some time and new arrivals.

If not possible to find a place of residence, please report to a municipality to ask for help and to register.  

In order to be covered by the Temporary Protection Directive, refugees from Ukraine need to be registered in the Personal Records Database (BRP) and get a residence sticker from the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND).

The appointment with the IND should be scheduled within 4 weeks from the date of the registration in the BRP.

Refugees from Ukraine are then entitled to accommodation, a subsistence allowance, healthcare and education.   

[*Dutch Government website*](https://www.government.nl/topics/reception-of-refugees-from-ukraine/arrival-registration-and-stay)

Document: Can I get shelter in the Netherlands if I am already registered in another Schengen country?

Yes, if you are registered in a Schengen country but you want to come to the Netherlands and apply for shelter here, please make sure you have the Ukrainian nationality or permanent residence permit, and you left Ukraine after 26th November, 2021.

Due to the current shortage of shelter places, there are no guarantees that a municipality will grant you shelter.

When you arrive to the Netherlands, please report to any municipality to try to register and receive shelter.

Document: What can I do when I am evicted or transferred from the shelter?

If the PA is entitled to a place at a municipal reception centre but was evicted or transferred to another shelter, collect information about the case.

How long did the PA stay there?

What was the reason for eviction?

Discuss the case with the Team Captain and forward PA also to the online consultation of RefugeeHelp: https://www.refugeehelp.nl/nl/ukrainian-refugee/appointment

Coming to the Netherlands for temporary treatment and then returning to Ukraine: Since the start of the war, the EU has designed a standard procedure for Ukrainians in need of urgent medical care.
